seo.title: Third-party plugins | OpenMixer
seo.description: Installing LV2 and CLAP plugins from your distribution, how plugin-hostd runs them and what a plugin-qualify verdict means for you.

hero.title: Plugins from your distribution, and what the console does with them.
hero.lede: The console runs LV2 and CLAP plugins that were not written for it. Each one runs in a process of its own, and each can be measured before a show, so you know in advance whether it is safe to rely on.

install.title: Install them from the distribution.
install.intro: A third-party plugin installs like any other package. As an example, the LSP plugin suite, in its LV2 and CLAP builds:
install.debian: On Debian and Raspberry Pi OS:
install.where: The files land in the distribution's plugin directories. On Debian that is /usr/lib/lv2 and /usr/lib/clap. On Fedora LV2 goes to /usr/lib64/lv2, and this suite's CLAP file goes to /usr/lib64/clap, not to /usr/lib/clap, where the omx plugins and the qualifier's default search look.

hostd.title: How the console runs them.
hostd.workers: plugin-hostd runs LV2 and CLAP plugins, each in a worker process of its own, behind the same socket protocol the console already speaks. Audio never passes through the daemon: every worker is an audio client of its own.
hostd.crash: If a plugin crashes, only its worker is restarted, with its settings put back, and the other plugins keep playing. A plugin that keeps crashing is singled out and given up on without touching its neighbours.
hostd.pins: Before a plugin starts, the daemon checks that its files are the ones that were checked: it hashes them and compares them with the plugin's recorded pin. A plugin updated or swapped behind your back is refused until you accept the new files, so a change cannot slip in unchecked. A plugin whose record says it was refused does not start.
hostd.picker: What the plugin picker offers on a channel is described in the {chapter}.

qualify.what: plugin-qualify scans a plugin, measures it offline (latency and CPU cost) and runs it under a real host, then gives one verdict. It installs next to plugin-hostd:

qualify.exit: The exit code is 0 when every plugin qualified, 1 when some did not and 2 when something could not be measured.
qualify.path: --all walks the CLAP search path (CLAP_PATH, then ~/.clap, then /usr/lib/clap) and refuses when LV2 bundles are installed, since it does not measure LV2 itself. In that case name the plugins or bundles.

verdicts.title: What a verdict means for you.
verdicts.intro: Four verdicts. The deciding reason is printed beside it.

suitable.text: Every check was made and passed. The plugin is safe to run inside the console's own engine process. This is the only verdict that counts as qualified.

conditional.text: It works, with a caution, for example a high cost at small buffer sizes. It is run isolated, and the reason names the caution.
conditional.do: Rack it if you can live with the reason, and read the reason first.

unknown.text: Something was not measured. An unmeasured plugin is never counted as a pass.
unknown.do: Measure it again, or leave it off the live rig.

unsuitable.text: A measured failure: a crash, a memory error in the plugin's own code, a real-time violation (it allocates memory, takes locks or makes system calls while it processes audio) or a required feature the host does not provide.
unsuitable.do: Leave it off the live rig.

verdicts.worst: The worst check decides the verdict.
verdicts.host: A verdict is judged for a particular host. The default is the console itself; the same measurements can be judged for other hosts, so a plugin can be fine in one and refused in another.
